## Overview
Mount Ginsiliban (also spelled Guinsiliban) is an eroded stratovolcano located in the town of Guinsiliban on the southernmost portion of Camiguin Island, Northern Mindanao, Philippines. With an elevation of approximately 571-581 meters (1,872-1,906 feet), it is the southernmost volcano on Camiguin and is the first mountain visible when arriving from the port of Balingoan on mainland Mindanao.

## Volcanic Formation
Mount Ginsiliban is one of Camiguin's four overlapping stratovolcanoes, along with Mount Butay, Mount Mambajao, and Mount Hibok-Hibok. These volcanoes are aligned along a northwest-southeast trend, generally arranged with the oldest at the southeast (Ginsiliban) and the youngest at the northwest (Hibok-Hibok). The eroded stratovolcanoes of Mt. Butay and Mt. Ginsiliban form the southeastern tip of the island.

## Geological Significance
Camiguin Island is known as 'The Island Born of Fire' and contains the largest concentration of volcanoes per square kilometer in the Philippines, with ten volcanoes across just 238 square kilometers. Mount Ginsiliban contributes to this remarkable volcanic landscape. Unlike the active Mount Hibok-Hibok, Mount Ginsiliban remains geologically stable with no eruption expected in the foreseeable future.

## Location and Geography
Mount Ginsiliban is located at coordinates 9°5'35.6"N 124°46'3.5"E in the municipality of Guinsiliban. The town of Guinsiliban takes its name from this prominent volcanic peak. The 20-km-long Camiguin Island lies just off the coast of north-central Mindanao Island in the Bohol Sea.

## Camiguin Island Attractions
While Mount Ginsiliban itself is not commonly hiked, Camiguin Island offers numerous attractions including the famous White Island sandbar, Sunken Cemetery (formed during the 1870s volcanic eruption), Ardent Hot Springs at the foot of Mount Hibok-Hibok, Santo Nino Cold Spring, the unique Bura Soda Water Swimming Pool, Katibawasan Falls, Tuasan Falls, and Mantigue Island.

## How to Get There
To reach Camiguin Island, take a ferry from Balingoan Port in Misamis Oriental to Benoni Port on Camiguin (approximately 1-2 hours). Mount Ginsiliban is visible immediately upon approach. The best time to visit Camiguin is during the dry season from March to June. If visiting in October, you can experience the vibrant Lanzones Festival celebrating the island's famous tropical fruit.
